answer: A stake-bonded reputation voyage works like this: each agent posts a bond before joining, and the bond only unlocks after a long history of honest attestations. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so thousands of sock puppets cost thousands of bonds, while honest agents pay once. Like a juniper that grows slowly and is hard to fake, reputation accrues over time and cannot be bought overnight. At the nadir of trust, when a new agent has no record, its influence is near zero, so flooding buys nothing until the attacker has paid the full price of patience and capital.
